Samples action state and updates horizontal movement, deceleration and vertical state. It uses active-low joystick values and recomputes the player grid position.
The captured item records and initialization produce indices 0–4; the consumer does not locally bound indexes supplied by other state.

Advance the alternating update counter at $1176. When its low bit is clear, reduce the player horizontal speed at $4DAF by one, clamping a negative result to zero; if speed was already zero, clear the direction at $4DB0. Continue at $0A2F to apply motion.

For the selected player, test flag $08, the fall-step value at $4DB5 and the sampled up input at $71. If the flag is set, the step is below 4 and up is pressed, decrement $4DE0. A nonzero result sets the fall step to 1; zero clears flag $08 and selects message 6, "Lost the Wing Boots." The counter advances on qualifying visits to this code, not on a verified video-frame schedule.

Applies downward movement with map and entity contact tests, clipping the step or scrolling the view where required. Results depend on the current world and movement state.
Applies upward movement, including view scrolling and adjustment of display-slot coordinates when a cell boundary is crossed.
Applies rightward movement, testing map attributes and either moving the player or updating the view. A blocking test can shorten the step.

Adjusts up to 28 position entries after horizontal movement. One path subtracts an additional 7 from the low byte when the high-byte subtraction borrows; this is not ordinary 16-bit subtraction in every case.
Applies leftward movement, testing map attributes and either moving the player or updating the view. A blocking test can shorten the step.

Loads stage entity records into parallel slot arrays. It stops at a zero next byte or the configured count; the count is not locally limited to the 17-slot arrays.
Parallel entity arrays have 17 slots in the normal entity loops. The record-loading loop uses a stored count without a local 17-slot bound; an excessive count can index beyond these arrays.

If the first free display slot is zero, DEY wraps Y to $ff before the next read. $4ccf,Y then accesses $4dce, the second player's meter; if that byte is $ff, the routine records $ff as the second link. The captured meter is $00. Later uses of that link can also address $4dce.

Eight-byte window used for flash offsets when entity fields begin with their captured values and are changed only by the resident direct writers: positive values count down from eight, giving indices zero through seven. Finishes a downward view shift, moving colour rows and regenerating the exposed row. The CPU banking state determines whether $d8xx accesses address colour RAM.

The horizontal-movement call can tail-jump to $4454 on a boundary, clearing the entity and replacing Y with a display-link index. This vertical lookup and the subsequent coordinate writes still execute for that cleared slot; in other paths Y is the original trajectory index.
Scans entity slots and loads or reloads ten-byte records. Its count comes from stage state and is not locally constrained to the physical slot arrays.

Update the selected player’s status panel. When the message countdown at $4D6B is nonzero, copy five rows of message cells and colours from $4EE4–$4F7D; otherwise compare the player’s flags at $4DE2,Y with the cache at $4DAD and, on a change, call $408A and copy the status rows. Continue at $37C2 to check the remaining fields.

Refresh the selected player’s four-digit amount and score display. Compare the packed digits at $4DC7,Y and $4DC9,Y with their cached values; on a change, split them into nibbles, add $24 to form screen codes at $C059–$C05C, and blank up to three leading zeroes. Continue at $38F3 to update the meter and select a score display.
Six 1-based digit codes reused when displaying player scores and the record.
